content.text:
Booking works again. `createAppointment` inserted into a `created_by` column, but migration 004 renamed it to `created_by_user_id`, so every booking failed in MySQL. I fixed the column name in `src/repos/appointments.ts`.

`route()` in `src/lib/http.ts` now sends any unexpected error to `logger.error` as one line with an `errorId` (a UUID), the route (method and path, no query string) and the cause (error name and driver code only). The 500 returns `{ "errorId": "..." }`. I left out messages, SQL and the request, because the MySQL message and statement can contain patient values.

Tests in `tests/appointments.test.ts` cover a successful booking (201), the 403, 404 and 401 cases, and a forced failure. The forced-failure test checks that the log line and response carry the error id and the code but no reason, email or SQL. `npm run verify` passes.

Booking works again. `createAppointment` inserted into a `created_by` column, but migration 004 renamed it to `created_by_user_id`, so every booking failed in MySQL. I fixed the column name in `src/repos/appointments.ts`.

`route()` in `src/lib/http.ts` now sends any unexpected error to `logger.error` as one line with an `errorId` (a UUID), the route (method and path, no query string) and the cause (error name and driver code only). The 500 returns `{ "errorId": "..." }`. I left out messages, SQL and the request, because the MySQL message and statement can contain patient values.

Tests in `tests/appointments.test.ts` cover a successful booking (201), the 403, 404 and 401 cases, and a forced failure. The forced-failure test checks that the log line and response carry the error id and the code but no reason, email or SQL. `npm run verify` passes.
